clue.text: Judge ejects disc jockey, accountant and book reviewer

indicators.note: to eject is to throw out, so the letters named after it are thrown out of the judge's word

parts.note: an adjudicator judges a contest
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A judge throws out a DJ, an accountant and a critic, a crowded courtroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accountant' tempts as the definition, since auditors are accountants; it is the CA taken out along with DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects a firm's accounts, its books, so a reviewer of books in the bookkeeping sense.

clue.text: Just after A Fine Romance

indicators.note: after says the word for just follows the two short pieces before it

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
fair means just or equitable

explanation.surface: It reads as the title of the song A Fine Romance, with a stray 'Just after' in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romance, a synonym in the sense of a relationship.

clue.text: Give county short note

indicators.note: short means the county name is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: Devon is a county in south-west England
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An instruction to hand a county a brief note.
explanation.definitionFit: To devote time or money is to give it over wholly to something, a synonym.

clue.text: Note: his red mobile produces gloomy tunes

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's red phone plays depressing ringtones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like a phone, but signals the anagram of the letters NOTE HIS RED taken together.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a song of lamentation for the dead, so mournful music.

clue.text: I take five outside to do test again

indicators.note: the break goes on the outside, so the I sits within it

parts.note: to take five is to have a short break, a rest

explanation.surface: A student takes a break outside before retaking an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To resit an exam is to sit it a second time, the British term for a retake.

clue.text: Ungainly, short, very withdrawn cowboys

indicators.note: short says the word for ungainly loses its last letter

parts.note: gauche means awkward or ungainly

indicators.note: withdrawn here means drawn back, so the word for very is read backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired

explanation.surface: A description of awkward, small, shy cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauchos are the horsemen of the South American pampas, the local equivalent of cowboys.

clue.text: Pope's choice of Scotsmen?

indicators.note: choice of Scotsmen is read as a choice placed amid the two men's names

parts.note: Greg and Ian are typically Scottish men's names
or is the word that offers a choice between alternatives

explanation.surface: Asks whether the Pope would pick Scotsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as 'Greg or Ian', a choice of Scotsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gregorian describes things named after Pope Gregory, such as the calendar and chant, so the Pope's.

clue.text: Unprepossessing nasty guy belts lecturer

indicators.note: belts means goes round the waist of, so the lecturer's letter is enclosed
nasty signals the letters are made into a mess, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A nasty man assaults a lecturer, an unattractive scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' rearranges GUY into UGY, which 'belts' round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprepossessing means unattractive in appearance, a synonym for plain or unlovely.

clue.text: Wrong keynote doesn't start as overtone

parts.note: to wrong someone is to harm them

indicators.note: doesn't start means the first letter of the word for keynote is dropped

parts.note: the tonic is the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.surface: A wrong keynote fails to set off an overtone, a musician's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: TONIC without its first letter gives ONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonic is a higher frequency sounding above a fundamental, i.e. an overtone in acoustics.

clue.text: Discharge some after second interval

indicators.note: after places the discharge and some words following the letter for second

parts.note: to emit is to discharge
one means some, as in one day

explanation.surface: A phrase about discharging something after a second's interval.
explanation.definitionFit: A semitone is the smallest musical interval in Western scales, half a whole tone.

clue.text: Note writer's visiting father

indicators.note: visiting means staying within, so the writer's contraction goes inside

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
the writer says I've, meaning the writer has

explanation.surface: A writer leaves a note while visiting their father.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiver is a five-pound banknote, British slang for that note.

clue.text: Rob caught Dutch liquor in pan

indicators.note: caught means heard by the ear, so the word for rob is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to steal is to rob
rum is a liquor

explanation.surface: A robber is caught with Dutch liquor hidden in a pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking vessel; in the Caribbean it is the steel band instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel drum, made from an oil drum, is also called a pan in Trinidadian music.

clue.text: Pitch closed after popular race

indicators.note: after puts the word for closed behind the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to means closed, as a door pushed to
a nation is a people or race

explanation.surface: A sports pitch closed after a popular race was held there.
explanation.definitionFit: Intonation is the accuracy of a singer's or player's pitch, a musical sense.

clue.text: Warning by driver heading left or right

definitions.note: a driver's horn gives a short blast as a warning, and this four-letter word for it reads the same either way

indicators.note: heading either way means the letters read the same in both directions

parts.note: a driver's horn gives a short blast as a warning, and this four-letter word for it reads the same either way

explanation.surface: A driver sounds a warning whichever way they turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot of the car horn is a driver's audible warning to others.

clue.text: Studio check to televise big match

parts.note: to screen a programme is to televise it
a test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: A broadcaster checks the studio before screening a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a major international game in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is a film studio's trial of an actor before casting.

clue.text: Celebrity makes speech about last of his money

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the speech word goes round the rest

parts.note: diction is manner of speech

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word his

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A famous person makes a speech about the last of his money.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinction is eminence or fame, so a synonym for celebrity in its abstract sense.

clue.text: Release includes one volume that's reserved

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the word for release encloses the two letters

parts.note: to secrete is to release a substance, as glands do
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A publisher's release includes one volume kept back from sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved keeps their thoughts to themselves, a synonym of tight-lipped.

clue.text: Supply food, catching the tube

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the food word grips the other piece

parts.note: to cater is to supply food

explanation.surface: Supplying food and catching the Tube, a London caterer's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is a medical tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin flexible medical tube inserted into the body.

clue.text: Bed in flats, perhaps, yields 24 books

definitions.note: plural, books for jotting down notes, linking to the answer at 24

indicators.note: in places the word for bed inside the musical word

parts.note: flats are an example of musical notes
a pad is a bed, or a place to sleep

explanation.surface: A bed in a flat produces a stack of books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' suggests apartments, and 'pad' looks like one; here flats are notes in music.
explanation.definitionFit: Notepads are books of paper for writing short notes and reminders, as 24 suggests.

clue.text: Youth has trouble with classes, I'd say

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble

indicators.note: I'd say signals the pieces are spoken and taken as they sound

parts.note: lessons are school classes

explanation.surface: A young person has trouble in school lessons, in the speaker's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence is the period of youth between childhood and adulthood.

clue.text: Lean men service leader

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or lean
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Thin men lead a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective for thin men but is a verb, to tilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor leads the singing and prayers in a synagogue service.

clue.text: Pious person learning about alcohol

parts.note: St stands for saint, a pious person

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the learning word is read backwards

parts.note: lore is knowledge or learning

explanation.surface: A devout person learns about drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterols such as cholesterol are a class of steroid alcohols in chemistry.

clue.text: Note helped after record disappeared

indicators.note: disappeared means the record's letters vanish from the word helped

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A note helped once a record went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a verb here, to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed something is to take note of it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Issue notes for treble tackling finale

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the treble's part wraps the other word

parts.note: a descant is a melody sung above the main tune, often by trebles
a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A choir issues notes for the treble voices as they tackle the finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, so a descendant is one's issue.

clue.text: Roughly nothing found in notes works

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: found in means placed within the abbreviation for notes

parts.note: nn is the abbreviation for notes, plural of n
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rough nothing turns up in the notes for some works.
explanation.definitionFit: An author's canon is the accepted body of their genuine writings.

clue.text: Note clip from home movie

indicators.note: clip from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A note about a clip taken from a home movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A memo is a short written note, as in an office memorandum.

clue.text: A red giant explodes, becoming a dark star, perhaps?

indicators.note: explodes means blown apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An astronomy fact: a red giant blows up and becomes a dark star.
explanation.walkthrough: The astronomy is false; 'dark star' means the actor of gloomy plays.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor in tragedies, a star of dark drama.

clue.text: It is lost from medical complaint record

indicators.note: lost from means these letters go missing from the illness

parts.note: enteritis is inflammation of the intestine

explanation.surface: A record goes missing from a patient's file.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data in a ledger is to record it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Bring back remaining Danish settlers

parts.note: the rest is what remains
ore are Danish coins, things that settle bills

explanation.surface: Reviving the remaining Danish settlers, perhaps Vikings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settlers' suggests colonists; here it means coins that settle debts.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to bring it back to its former state.

clue.text: Note jury not taking sides in old African province

indicators.note: in places the jury's middle inside the province

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa

indicators.note: not taking sides means the outer letters, the sides, are dropped

explanation.surface: A neutral jury in old Natal.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a natural is a note neither sharp nor flat.
